scope: Interlude3stage2; citations support specific claims, not a complete rereading of every work

notes.locator: Original article, p. 115, complexity at minimum component cost
notes.source_note: Gordon E. Moore, [“Cramming More Components onto Integrated Circuits”](https://download.intel.com/newsroom/2023/manufacturing/moores-law-electronics.pdf), *Electronics* 38(8), 19 April 1965, pp. 114–117. The forecast concerns complexity at minimum component cost and projects the annual trend for another decade. It is an economic and technological projection, not a physical law.

notes.limits: No claim that von Neumann alone invented the computer or named the field.
notes.source_note: John von Neumann, [*First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC*](https://library.si.edu/digital-library/book/firstdraftofrepo00vonn), 30 June 1945, §§2.2–2.6. The report describes central arithmetic, control, memory and input/output. The project and stored-program design were collaborative; the report’s single-author circulation should not erase J. Presper Eckert and John Mauchly.

MIT, [*Computation Structures*, lecture 13, “Building the Beta”](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-004-computation-structures-spring-2017/pages/c13/c13s1/) (Spring 2017), especially “Multi-ported Register File,” “ALU Instructions” and “Instruction Fetch/Decode.” The addition and figure here are original simplified examples, not a timing diagram for a particular commercial processor.

MIT, [*Computation Structures*, lecture 9, “Designing an Instruction Set”](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-004-computation-structures-spring-2017/pages/c9/c9s1/); John L. Hennessy and David A. Patterson, [“A New Golden Age for Computer Architecture”](https://www.doc.ic.ac.uk/~wl/teachlocal/arch/papers/cacm19golden-age.pdf), *Communications of the ACM* 62(2) (2019), pp. 48–60, especially pp. 48–51 on ISAs, implementations and microprogramming.

notes.locator: Lecture14 locality and hit/miss passages; lecture13 enabled registers
notes.source_note: MIT, [*Computation Structures*, lecture 14, “Caches and the Memory Hierarchy”](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-004-computation-structures-spring-2017/pages/c14/c14s1/), on SRAM, DRAM, locality and cache hits/misses; lecture 13 for register retention. Cache organization varies by processor; the figure presents roles, not a universal physical layout.

notes.locator: MIT course pipeline content; Spectre intro pp1–3
notes.verification: Spectre primary background checked; MIT course allocation checked
notes.source_note: MIT, [*Computation Structures*, lecture 15, “Pipelining the Beta”](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-004-computation-structures-spring-2017/pages/c15/c15s1/); Paul Kocher et al., [“Spectre Attacks”](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.01203) (2018 preprint), introduction and processor background, for branch prediction and speculative execution. Pipelining improves throughput; misprediction penalties depend on the implementation.

notes.claim: Approximate brain metabolic budget; communication costs
notes.locator: Energy Audit and discussion of20W vsATP costs
notes.source_note: William B. Levy and Victoria G. Calvert, [“Communication Consumes 35 Times More Energy than Computation in the Human Cortex, but Both Costs Are Needed to Predict Synapse Number”](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8106317/), *PNAS* 118(18) (2021), e2008173118. Their energy audit discusses the customary approximately 20-W whole-brain figure and the distinction between metabolic supply, signaling and computation. The precise partition depends on the model; no universal brain/computer efficiency ranking is inferred.

notes.claim: 4096 discrepancy; probable bit inversion distinct from cosmic cause
notes.verification: Indexed full official report passage and IBM primary abstract checked
notes.source_note: Belgian parliamentary College of Experts, [2003 election report](https://www.dekamer.be/FLWB/pdf/51/0001/51K0001002.pdf), DOC 51 0001/002, §§5.3.7.1–5.3.7.2, p. 22: the 4,096-vote discrepancy is consistent with a spontaneous inversion of the counter’s thirteenth bit. The report does not establish a cosmic-ray cause. For radiation-induced errors, J. F. Ziegler et al., [“IBM Experiments in Soft Fails in Computer Electronics (1978–1994)”](https://research.ibm.com/publications/ibm-experiments-in-soft-fails-in-computer-electronics-1978-1994), *IBM Journal of Research and Development* 40(1) (1996), pp. 3–18.

notes.verification: Manufacturer document and indexed relevant passage checked
notes.source_note: Intel, [*Processor Datasheet*, volume 1, document 743844, revision 015](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/743844/743844-015.pdf) (May 2025), §2.7, “Clock Topology,” describes separate clock domains. Zilog’s manual below illustrates clocked state transitions in an earlier architecture.

notes.claim: Z80 cycle counts, branches and waits
notes.source_note: Zilog, [*Z80 CPU User Manual*](https://www.zilog.com/docs/z80/um0080.pdf), UM008011-0816 (2016), “Timing” and individual instruction descriptions. T-states are clock periods; conditional paths and inserted WAIT states can change elapsed execution time. The classroom Sord model remains unconfirmed, so it is not assigned a processor here.

notes.locator: Primary review abstract; monograph retained as further reading
notes.verification: Review abstract checked; not a full reread of2006book
notes.source_note: György Buzsáki and Andreas Draguhn, [“Neuronal Oscillations in Cortical Networks”](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15218136/), *Science* 304 (2004), pp. 1926–1929, doi:10.1126/science.1099745. See also Buzsáki, *Rhythms of the Brain* (Oxford University Press, 2006). Frequency bands and functional associations vary across species, regions and behavioral states.

Guo-qiang Bi and Mu-ming Poo, [“Synaptic Modifications in Cultured Hippocampal Neurons: Dependence on Spike Timing, Synaptic Strength, and Postsynaptic Cell Type”](https://www.gatsby.ucl.ac.uk/~pel/course_wuhan/papers/bi.poo_1998.pdf), *Journal of Neuroscience* 18(24) (1998), pp. 10464–10472, doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.18-24-10464.1998. The experimental conditions and cell types matter; the before/after rule is not a universal law of synapses.

notes.locator: Primary paper abstract and indexed discussion
notes.verification: Primary abstract and indexed paper passages checked
notes.source_note: John O’Keefe and Michael L. Recce, [“Phase Relationship between Hippocampal Place Units and the EEG Theta Rhythm”](https://doi.org/10.1002/hipo.450030307), *Hippocampus* 3(3) (1993), pp. 317–330. The relation is between position within a firing field and spike phase, not a single universal clock coordinate for the animal.

notes.claim: Sleep sequence replay and temporal compression
notes.verification: Primary indexed paper passages and metadata checked
notes.source_note: William E. Skaggs and Bruce L. McNaughton, [“Replay of Neuronal Firing Sequences in Rat Hippocampus during Sleep Following Spatial Experience”](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8596957/), *Science* 271 (1996), pp. 1870–1873; Zoltán Nádasdy et al., [“Replay and Time Compression of Recurring Spike Sequences in the Hippocampus”](https://www.jneurosci.org/content/jneuro/19/21/9497.full.pdf), *Journal of Neuroscience* 19(21) (1999), pp. 9497–9507. “Rehearsing” is an explanatory image; these observations alone do not establish every function of replay.

notes.verification: Indexed original argument and later author retrospective checked; direct Berkeley PDF unavailable
notes.source_note: David A. Patterson and David R. Ditzel, [“The Case for the Reduced Instruction Set Computer”](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~kubitron/courses/cs252-F00/handouts/papers/patterson80.pdf), *ACM SIGARCH Computer Architecture News* 8(6) (1980), pp. 25–33. For earlier IBM work and the later convergence of implementations, see Hennessy and Patterson, “A New Golden Age,” pp. 50–53. Instruction-set labels alone do not predict energy efficiency.

notes.claim: End of easy voltage scaling and power-limited clocks
notes.source_note: Hennessy and Patterson, [“A New Golden Age for Computer Architecture”](https://www.doc.ic.ac.uk/~wl/teachlocal/arch/papers/cacm19golden-age.pdf), pp. 53–54, “End of Moore’s Law and Dennard Scaling.” Transistor count, voltage scaling, clock frequency and useful performance are distinct trends; multicore designs did not remove power or communication limits.

notes.claim: Two-GPU AlexNet training and image-recognition advance
notes.source_note: Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever and Geoffrey E. Hinton, [“ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks”](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2012/file/c399862d3b9d6b76c8436e924a68c45b-Paper.pdf), *Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems* 25 (2012), especially §3.2, “Training on Multiple GPUs,” and §6. The two devices were NVIDIA GTX 580 GPUs.

notes.claim: SMs, threads, warps, divergence and Tensor Cores
notes.source_note: NVIDIA, [*GPU Performance Background User’s Guide*](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/performance/dl-performance-gpu-background/index.html), §§2–3, and [*CUDA Programming Guide*, “Warps and SIMT”](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/01-introduction/programming-model.html#warps-and-simt). A warp has 32 threads; divergent paths reduce active-lane utilization. Tensor Cores specialize in matrix operations, while other units perform surrounding work.

notes.claim: Weighted sums, tiled products and reuse
notes.source_note: NVIDIA, [*Matrix Multiplication Background User’s Guide*](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/performance/dl-performance-matrix-multiplication/index.html), §§1 and 2.1; [*Blackwell Tuning Guide*](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/blackwell-tuning-guide/index.html), memory-system discussion. The numerical example and diagram are original. Actual staging can use shared memory, registers and generation-specific matrix storage; the diagram is not a literal B200 block diagram.

NVIDIA, [*GPU Performance Background User’s Guide*, “Understanding Performance” and “DNN Operation Categories”](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/performance/dl-performance-gpu-background/index.html), and [*Matrix Multiplication Background User’s Guide*, “Math and Memory Bounds”](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/performance/dl-performance-matrix-multiplication/index.html). Arithmetic intensity compares operations with transferred bytes at a specified memory boundary. Batching, dimensions, kernels and hardware determine the actual bottleneck.

notes.claim: B200: two dies, 208 billion transistors and documented 180 GB capacity
notes.limits: Dated B200example, not all products bearing Blackwellname; no vendor speedup generalized.
notes.source_note: NVIDIA, [Blackwell architecture](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/technologies/blackwell-architecture/) and [*Blackwell Tuning Guide*, §1.4.2.1](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/blackwell-tuning-guide/index.html): two reticle-limited compute dies, approximately 208 billion transistors and up to 180 GB of B200 HBM capacity. The initial 2024 announcement listed 192 GB; the main text uses the documented usable capacity rather than mixing configurations.

notes.locator: Articleformat table and What isNVFP4 body, notgeneratedsummary
notes.source_note: Eduardo Alvarez et al., NVIDIA, [“Introducing NVFP4 for Efficient and Accurate Low-Precision Inference”](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/introducing-nvfp4-for-efficient-and-accurate-low-precision-inference/) (24 June 2025), format table and scaling discussion. Low-bit values can require additional scale metadata; not every training quantity or accumulation uses the same precision.

notes.claim: Rubin announced memory specification, not shipment date
notes.limits: Announced limits, not measured application performance; avoid stale latest/workhorseclaims.
notes.source_note: Kyle Aubrey, NVIDIA, [“Inside the NVIDIA Vera Rubin Platform: Six New Chips, One AI Supercomputer”](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/inside-the-nvidia-rubin-platform-six-new-chips-one-ai-supercomputer/) (5 January 2026; subsequently updated), “Memory and Decode Efficiency”: up to 288 GB HBM4 and 22 TB/s per GPU. These are manufacturer specifications. The passage makes no claim that every announced system was shipping on that date.

notes.verification: Bibliographicrecord checked; explanatory passages verified in citedteaching/manufacturer sources
notes.limits: UVAfulltext blocked; no quotations or exactperformancepredictions takenfromunreadreport.
notes.source_note: Wm. A. Wulf and Sally A. McKee, [“Hitting the Memory Wall: Implications of the Obvious”](https://libraopen.library.virginia.edu/entities/publication/a6907010-027d-405e-8f0b-4707e1263ad9), University of Virginia report CS-94-48 (1994), later *ACM SIGARCH Computer Architecture News* 23(1) (1995), pp. 20–24. MIT’s memory-hierarchy lecture and NVIDIA’s performance guides above explain how locality and bandwidth affect present designs.

International Energy Agency, [*Energy and AI*, “Energy Demand from AI”](https://www.iea.org/reports/energy-and-ai/energy-demand-from-ai) (2025), “The Outlook for Energy Demand from Data Centres”: approximately 415 TWh and 1.5% of global electricity in 2024. This is total data-center electricity, not an estimate of AI alone.

Paul Kocher et al., [“Spectre Attacks: Exploiting Speculative Execution”](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.01203) (2018 preprint; *IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy*, 2019); Moritz Lipp et al., [“Meltdown: Reading Kernel Memory from User Space”](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/conference/usenixsecurity18/sec18-lipp.pdf), *USENIX Security* (2018), pp. 973–990. Both became public in January 2018. Their transient-execution mechanisms differ, as do affected processors.

Chris Olah et al., [“Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits”](https://distill.pub/2020/circuits/zoom-in/), *Distill* (2020), doi:10.23915/distill.00024.001; Catherine Olsson et al., [“In-context Learning and Induction Heads”](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.11895) (2022). Curve detectors and induction heads are specific interpretability findings, not a complete explanation of all vision or language models.

AMD Adaptive Computing, [“From Invention to AI Acceleration: Celebrating 40 Years of FPGA Innovation”](https://www.amd.com/en/blogs/2025/from-invention-to-ai-acceleration--celebrating-40-years-of-fpga-.html) (2 June 2025), identifies the Xilinx XC2064, introduced in 1985, as the first commercial FPGA. Configuration changes logic and routing through manufactured resources; it does not grow new transistors.

Grzegorz Rozenberg, Thomas Bäck and Joost N. Kok, eds., [*Handbook of Natural Computing*](https://link.springer.com/referencework/10.1007/978-3-540-92910-9) (Springer, 2012), introduction and overview of the field’s strands. Nature-inspired algorithms, modeling natural processes and computing with physical/biological substrates are related but distinct projects. The proposed shifting of abstraction boundaries is my question.

notes.claim: Conductance weights, current sums and total-system costs
notes.source_note: Manuel Le Gallo et al., [“A 64-Core Mixed-Signal In-Memory Compute Chip Based on Phase-Change Memory for Deep Neural Network Inference”](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41928-023-01010-1), *Nature Electronics* 6 (2023), pp. 680–693, especially Extended Data Fig. 2 and the mixed-signal architecture. Conductance encoding and current summation require supporting digital operations, conversion and communication. This is a demonstrated inference chip, not a self-growing general intelligence.

notes.claim: Quantum simulation precedent; attractors and sampling; 2024 Nobel
notes.source_note: Richard P. Feynman, [“Simulating Physics with Computers”](https://authors.library.caltech.edu/records/a1kgk-xyk45), *International Journal of Theoretical Physics* 21 (1982), pp. 467–488; J. J. Hopfield, [“Neural Networks and Physical Systems with Emergent Collective Computational Abilities”](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC346238/), *PNAS* 79 (1982), pp. 2554–2558; David H. Ackley, Geoffrey E. Hinton and Terrence J. Sejnowski, “A Learning Algorithm for Boltzmann Machines,” *Cognitive Science* 9 (1985), pp. 147–169. See the [2024 Physics Nobel’s scientific background](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2024/popular-information/). The mathematical energy in these models is not automatically physical energy consumption.

notes.claim: Trainable physical systems as a foothold
notes.source_note: Logan G. Wright et al., [“Deep Physical Neural Networks Trained with Backpropagation”](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-021-04223-6), *Nature* 601 (2022), pp. 549–555. The demonstrated physics-aware training combines physical forward operations with a differentiable model for training. Continuous physical growth and an architecture that chooses its own abstraction boundaries are further conjectures, not results of this experiment.
